findings.one_line: The proof extends the pure-shift/four-corner identity from its stipulated square-integrable product domain to arbitrary pairs in Phi_P, but Phi_P requires only the total scores to be L2; the separate F, G, and R products can fail to be L2 while their displayed sum is L2, so C_P need not equal the closed span of all score differences.

Its claim that every bridge score is a gradient and that every gradient lies in A_P uses the false unrestricted normal-affine identity; absent a product-integrability restriction (or a redefinition using the closed span of actual score differences), the asserted quotient canonical-gradient characterization is not established.

The conditional sub-exponential bounds are imposed directly on training-determined squared learned dictionary and score products, but no primitive learner/tail conditions derive or demonstrate their achievability; the L4 and residual-rate assumptions do not imply them, so this estimator-side concentration premise must be discharged or the inference claim explicitly re-scoped to a verified bounded/sub-exponential learner regime.

cited_checks.note: The supplied Proposition 2.27 is the vector Lindeberg--Feller theorem; specializing to scalar mean-zero Y_{n,i}=X_{ni} makes its covariance condition sum E[X_{ni}^2] -> V and gives exactly the node conclusion.
